title: Preposition Orchard
intro: Depend ON, listen TO, arrive AT: dependent prepositions that no rule explains, only memory. Match each word with the preposition it always takes.

A2.why: Spanish “escuchar música” has no preposition, but English needs “to” before what you hear.
Spanish “mirar” takes nothing, so this “at” is easy to forget.
Wait FOR, never “wait the bus”: Spanish “esperar” hides the preposition.
Arrive AT a building or point, IN a city or country; never “arrive to”.
Good AT a skill, not “good in”: “She’s good at maths.”
Afraid OF, like “miedo de”: one of the friendly ones for Spanish speakers.
Interested IN, never “interested on”: “interesado en” helps you here.
Married TO someone, not “married with”: Spanish “casado con” is the trap.
Belong TO someone: “This horse belongs to the sheriff”, never “belongs of”.
Think ABOUT a topic, not “think in”: Spanish “pensar en” is the trap.
Proud OF someone, not “proud for”: here “orgulloso de” matches nicely.
Pay FOR the thing you buy: “We paid for the paella”, not “paid the paella”.

B1.why: Depend ON, never “depend of”: Spanish “depender de” is the classic trap.
Apologise TO a person FOR the thing you did.
Believe IN an idea or person you trust; Spanish “creer en” matches.
Worry ABOUT a problem; “preocuparse por” tempts Spanish speakers into “worry for”.
Complain ABOUT the problem, and TO the person who can fix it.
Succeed IN something, or IN doing it; never “succeed to do”.
Congratulate someone ON their success, not “for”: “felicitar por” is the trap.
Insist ON + -ing: “He insisted on paying”, never “insisted to pay”.
Agree WITH a person or opinion: “estar de acuerdo con” matches.
Laugh AT a joke or person, not “laugh of”: Spanish “reírse de” is the trap.
Suffer FROM an illness: “She suffers from migraines”, not “suffers of”.
Search FOR what you want to find: prospectors searched for gold in California.

B2.why: Rely ON someone, just like “depend on”; never “rely in”.
Consist OF its parts; Spanish “consistir en” pulls you towards “in”.
Blame someone FOR a mistake, or blame the mistake ON someone.
Deal WITH a problem means handle it; don’t drop the “with”.
You always cope WITH something: “She coped with the pain.”
Benefit FROM something: the help comes FROM it.
React TO something that happens, never “react at”.
Specialise IN a field: “especializarse en” matches, so this one is friendly.
Object TO + noun or -ing: “The ranchers objected to the new railway.”
Accuse someone OF a crime, but charge them WITH it.
Participate IN an event: “participar en” matches; never “participate on”.
Recover FROM an illness or operation: you come back FROM it.

C1.why: Comply WITH rules or orders; the noun keeps it too: “in compliance with”.
Refrain FROM + noun or -ing: “Please refrain from smoking.”
Embark ON a journey or project, like stepping ON board a ship.
Adhere TO rules or a plan, like glue sticking TO a surface.
Capitalise ON a chance means use it to your advantage.
Grapple WITH a hard problem, like wrestling WITH it.
A problem stems FROM its cause, as a plant grows FROM its root.
Culminate IN a final high point: “The campaign culminated in victory.”
Abstain FROM voting or drinking; “abstenerse de” leads to the mistake “abstain of”.
Dispose OF means get rid of: hospitals must dispose of used needles safely.
Subscribe TO a magazine, or TO an idea you agree with.
Dwell ON the past means keep thinking about it too much.
